1400349717058318336 [2021-06-03] @AskYatharth 💜 21
My brain: “I’m judging every move I make 100% of the time.”

No wonder it can be exhausting to be around me.
↓
1400349717834334209 [2021-06-03] @AskYatharth 💜 8
Maybe other people are not like that.

But young neurotic types—there was intense introspection, intense comparison to a standard, evaluation for rightness, every second of being alive and awake.

https://t.co/JfdHZzNciT
  [Quoting @AskYatharth: @CountJ0ecool THANK YOU FOR articulating this.   “People don’t think about you as much as you do. They don’t think about you at all.”   *meanwhile judging everyone in the room and myself a lot on everything they’re doing]
↓
1400349718677385218 [2021-06-03] @AskYatharth 💜 5
Anyone who connects with me in intensity will feel that scrutiny. If not on them, then on me myself. 

No wonder it can be exhausting to connect with me.
↓
1400349719830794241 [2021-06-03] @AskYatharth 💜 5
I bring presence and connection every single moment.

It can be a good thing, but it can be exhausting to be under so much scrutiny, especially for someone new to it, especially for a woman already under constant scrutiny.
↓
1400349720548044802 [2021-06-03] @AskYatharth 💜 7 [(SEED) type=semantic_search]
Compare with connecting with someone who’s just vibing. Unconsciously chill, and they just . . . inspire a companionate simplicity.
↓
1400349721290412035 [2021-06-03] @AskYatharth 💜 7
There is a simplicity to being with them. 

There’s such a simple positive self-regard and a being of what one is.

No second-order emotions. Or if they are, they are there directly.

It’s refreshing and inviting in a neurotic world.
↓
1400349721957257219 [2021-06-03] @AskYatharth 💜 6
Neurotic = to have thoughts about thoughts.

For it to not short-circuit.

https://t.co/AepefKvS3E

What they feel, you are touched by.

https://t.co/I2XTZPslzB

A lot of conversations in my head recently have been like:

😖: fuck fuck fuck i really should go running. i feel crappy and i know they me feel better
🙆‍♀️: oh?

===

1421702217111834626 [2021-08-01] @AskYatharth 💜 13 🔁 1
😅: yes! that’d be great, thank you . . [relieved]
😔: it’s just . . . [wince] . . . it can be so hard to remember what i want . . . [wince] . . . when that super-ego part is yelling in my ear about what needs to be done, and then i feel sad, & confused, & don’t know what i want
↓
1421702220068831235 [2021-08-01] @AskYatharth 💜 13
🙆‍♀️: you got it, babe. i get you
🙆‍♀️: it didn’t feel safe for you to override parts of your brain, till you’d really understood on some high-level, how it was safe to, because your thoughts and brain were all you had
☹️: yeahh . . . https://t.co/HDK1aJe2Al
  [Quoting @AskYatharth: It’s worth not psy-op’ing these neurotic nerds [psy-op = get people to distrust their native trust mechanisms] by yelling “JUST BE” “YOU’RE THE PROBLEM” “THERE IS NO SUCH THING AS SELF-COERCION.”   They might temporarily feel better, but the ecological homeostasis will return.]
↓
1421702223273283585 [2021-08-01] @AskYatharth 💜 9
🙆‍♀️: and it feels really safe, now that you can — just let go of thoughts about the past and future and this and that, without resolving them, and return to the truth & clarity of this moment, of what you want
😊: hell yeah!!
🙆‍♀️: and what you want rn is to go running, right?
↓
1421702225643048962 [2021-08-01] @AskYatharth 💜 4
😀: yes!
🙆‍♀️: so let’s go . . first we get out stuff cleaned, and . . .—

that’s how it goes
↓
1421704166100062209 [2021-08-01] @AskYatharth 💜 21
What I’m learning to do is tease apart my ego & super-ego.

I grew up with a very hyper-developed sense of super-ego.

- Always a sense of the right thing to be done
- Very little connection with what *I want* to do. https://t.co/miKVtBS5GN
  [Quoting @AskYatharth: having a hyper-developed super-ego and under-developed ego is the definition of a Rules person  always looking for the right thing to do  little connection with what they actually want  https://t.co/aV0QXy0k23]
↓
1421705512727482371 [2021-08-01] @AskYatharth 💜 14
It led me to be a very neurotic person, always questioning what I’m doing, and having second thoughts, and third-order thoughts.

Everything getting passed through the sieve & filter of “Is this right? Is this what is supposed to be happening?” https://t.co/bZvkgmA3KI
  [Quoting @AskYatharth: @CountJ0ecool THANK YOU FOR articulating this.   “People don’t think about you as much as you do. They don’t think about you at all.”   *meanwhile judging everyone in the room and myself a lot on everything they’re doing]
↓
1421705630809788417 [2021-08-01] @AskYatharth 💜 7
What’s amazing to me about this kind of conversation is how kind it felt. 

The unkind thing to do—and the advice I heard all my life—was to JUST DO IT>

🧘‍♂️: just let go of thinking
🏋️‍♂️: just go lifting

but why?? did it feel safe to do that? https://t.co/Ap7eCUsPRf
  [Quoting @AskYatharth: Phrase considered harmful:     ”Just do it.”]
↓
1421710783109640192 [2021-08-01] @AskYatharth 💜 5
I needed to not psy-op myself into “fuhgedding about it” like a normie might be comfortable doing.

I really, really wanted to know if what I was doing was the right thing to be doing. https://t.co/HOFrusKv14
  [Quoting @AskYatharth: Where normies are fine just picking an action, neurotic nerds have a really strong expectation that the conflict shouldn’t be there, and there should be some sort of resolution. They’re so sensitive to internal expectation error they start whole Twitter communities about coercion]
↓
1421710786804715521 [2021-08-01] @AskYatharth 💜 5
I don’t blame the “JUST DO IT” advicers. It works for a lot of ppl. It didn’t for me. It just made me cry more on the inside

My problem wasn’t that I couldnt “JUST DO IT”

My problem was I’d been “JUST DOING IT” whtvr my super-ego told me was the right thing to do my entire life
↓
1421714183322746887 [2021-08-01] @AskYatharth 💜 5
What was kind was helping me move from where my existing trust function was.

My existing trust function was: I needed to know what I was doing was right.

So I helped myself come to an understanding of what was going on that made it feel safe to ignore my super-ego parts.
↓
1421714187361865734 [2021-08-01] @AskYatharth 💜 3 [(SEED) type=quote_of_semantic_search]
Once that felt safe, I could just vibe . . . 

But if it didn’t feel safe, goddamit—it could at best be a performance of vibing. https://t.co/MTkNDh8WZk
  [Quoting @AskYatharth: Compare with connecting with someone who’s just vibing. Unconsciously chill, and they just . . . inspire a companionate simplicity.]
↓
1421714194995589123 [2021-08-01] @AskYatharth 💜 3
So I came to this high-level consent in my system, that is was OKAY to let go of the super-ego parts, and once it was, I could do it.

Otherwise, *I AM LITERALLY TRYING TO DO SOMETHING MY HIGH-LEVEL SYSTEM HAS NOT CONSENTED TO DO* because everyone is saying to do it. https://t.co/3Tr92hLYp7
  [Quoting @AskYatharth: “I’m a 9.” “Oh, ok, let’s go with your opinion then.”  What just happened? It’s incredible. A laser-fast decision, WITHOUT sitting down and resolving all objections. Yet done non-coercively.]
↓
1421714198388744193 [2021-08-01] @AskYatharth 💜 2
That is not cool. https://t.co/lc8tkd4qFJ
  [Quoting @AskYatharth: Meditation doesn’t work (letting go of thought) if you don’t on some level WANT to let go of thought, aren’t bought in.]
↓
1421714207087763458 [2021-08-01] @AskYatharth 💜 7 🔁 1
One of my biggest talking points is that it is cruel to try to get yourself to understand something in a way that bypasses your trust mechanisms. https://t.co/zzf1Qyn6hV
  [Quoting @AskYatharth: It’s cruel to ask someone to get something in a way that bypasses their trust mechanisms.]
↓
1421714212720713733 [2021-08-01] @AskYatharth 💜 4
People in the past didn’t know how to explain it to you that way, but it’s okay.

It’s dumb to try to brutalise yourself with more Rules if you are already a Rules person.

You have no other way to relate to advice like “JUST DO IT” or “just let go.” https://t.co/BQdIENyPpa
  [Quoting @AskYatharth: Trial-by-fire is awesome, but ALSO it can lead to overly rigid people just brutalising themselves more with more sense of Rules, in a way that can be gentler, more deft, and more expansive. https://t.co/XGUtpudYlw]
↓
1421714216604602369 [2021-08-01] @AskYatharth 💜 3
Hopefully I’m plugging in one of the holes for you, like I am for me, about *why it’s okay* to let go super-ego parts, so you can consent to it, so you can do it, whole-heartedly, without drama.
↓
1421714859356524548 [2021-08-01] @AskYatharth 💜 4
before: felt unsafe to override a part
now: high-level consent

all this possible because i had a SAFE meeting where i realised super-ego voice i didn’t identify with and felt good letting go off

↓
1514228658709602305 [2022-04-13] @RichDecibels 💜 55 🔁 2

1514229166841155584 [2022-04-13] @RichDecibels 💜 52
